entries.claim: The new receipt guard runs only when all three settled figures are present, leaving a reasonless settlement able to bypass the guard by omitting any one figure.
entries.failure_scenario: A caller appends a settlement outcome for a record containing an overridden survived blocker, supplies no reason, and omits one settled figure. The plan explicitly skips the new check, so `appendEvent` still runs and the reasonless receipt is recorded, violating AC3 and the requirement that the self-asserted override be backed by a receipt.

entries.claim: The planned join tests only whether the receipt has any reason, not whether it is the corresponding `override` receipt required by the success criterion and documented accepted shape.
entries.failure_scenario: A `gate_pass` settlement over an overridden blocker supplies an unrelated non-empty detail file. Because `detail` is non-empty, the planned check accepts it even though no `override` receipt exists; the trace can therefore claim a clean pass for a record that still contains a survived blocker/high.

counter_evidence.note: D-04 locks the refusal shape: it is phrased as a record/receipt contradiction and NEVER keyed on an event name, so a check that distinguishes an override receipt from a gate_pass one is the coupling that decision rejects. cadence-core/bin/planning/trace.mjs:870-875 states the seam carries no runtime refusal keyed to an event name. ROADMAP success criterion 2 admits either OQ-1 resolution provided the accepted shape is stated in references/triage-gate.md, which plan task 5 does.

entries.claim: The end-to-end fixture does not require the malformed `fix_commit` to be on a `downgraded` or `refuted` entry, so it can pass while exercising only the already-covered survived-ruling refusal.
entries.failure_scenario: The executor places `fix_commit: 'not-a-sha'` on the survived entry and valid or absent values on the downgraded/refuted entries. The pre-phase implementation already refuses that payload, so the advertised end-to-end reproduction does not prove criterion 1's new non-survived path even though every Task 4 assertion can pass.
